steps.title: A recital with two touches
steps.body:
Same shape as every recital so far: two pieces, names said, hands in frame, one question from the family. This time, listen for whether staccato and legato are both audible in your playing, not just marked on the page.

1. Choose two pieces, one with clear articulation to show off, one older.
2. Run each once a day, exaggerating staccato and legato slightly so they carry to the back of the room.
3. Say the slip plan out loud before you play: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar.
4. On recital day, say each name, play, hold the last note, and bow.
5. The family asks one question. Answer it, then write the Practice log.

A listener who cannot tell staccato from legato in your playing is hearing correct notes but not yet hearing music.

figure.alt: A bar of four beats ending in a held note, matching the checklist's own line: last note held, hands off, then a bow.

steps.title: Recital checklist
steps.body: Tick each one before recital day.
checklist: Two pieces chosen, one with clear articulation to show, one older
Each piece run once a day, staccato and legato both exaggerated slightly
Slip plan said out loud: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar
Last note held, hands off, then a bow
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record both pieces in one take, names said out loud, phone where it sees the hands. Slips stay in.
